faqs.q: What is an alloy Grade 80 lashing hook and what is it used for?
faqs.a: The alloy Grade 80 lashing hook is a drop-forged, powder-coated end fitting for chain tie-downs that secure a load for transport. It is listed in one size, 1 t, and is not for overhead lifting. See the [Load Binders shelf](/c/load-binders) for the other binder parts.

faqs.q: How do I read the Indus part number on the alloy lashing hook Grade 80, for example IH-LR-LB-ALHG80-1T?
faqs.a: In IH-LR-LB-ALHG80-1T, the suffix 1T identifies the 1 t size, and IH-LR-LB-ALHG80-1T ends in 1T for 1 t. Every size in the size table has its own part number, so quote the one from the table.

faqs.q: What are the working load limit and breaking load of the Grade 80 alloy lashing hook?
faqs.a: The 1 t size has a working load limit of 1 t and a minimum breaking load of 4 t. The ratings use a 4:1 design factor between working load limit and minimum breaking load. Select on the working load limit, not the breaking load.

faqs.q: Which chain does the alloy Grade 80 lashing hook suit, and what are its dimensions?
faqs.a: Match the hook to the chain size and select on working load limit. The size table lists one 1 t size weighing 1.23 kg. It is a small lashing hook, so check its rating against the tie-down chain before ordering.

faqs.q: What is the Grade 80 alloy lashing hook made of, and how is it finished?
faqs.a: It is drop-forged alloy steel with a powder-coated finish. Grade 80 refers to the alloy chain grade the hook is intended to be used with. Ask us if you need another finish or material.

faqs.q: Does the Grade 80 alloy lashing hook come with a test certificate?
faqs.a: Yes. Each consignment ships with the manufacturer's test certificate. The facts we hold do not name a standard or third-party certification, so say on the RFQ if your site needs anything more, such as witnessed proof testing.

faqs.q: What chain and load binder can I use with the 1 t alloy lashing hook?
faqs.a: The hook fits a Grade 80 chain tie-down tensioned by a load binder, such as the [ratchet load binder](/p/ratchet-load-binder) or [lever load binder](/p/lever-load-binder). Check that the chain, hook and binder ratings suit the load before use.

faqs.q: Can the Grade 80 alloy lashing hook be used for overhead lifting?
faqs.a: No. It is listed as not for overhead lifting; its 1 t rating is a tie-down rating for load securing. Use a rated lifting component for a lift, and ask us which one fits your load.

faqs.q: Alloy lashing hook Grade 80 compared with the lashing type C hook with spring pin: which is right?
faqs.a: This 1 t alloy hook is the smaller part. The [Grade 80 lashing type C hook with spring pin](/p/grade-80-lashing-type-c-hook-with-spring-pin) is the larger part in three sizes and adds a spring pin. Choose on the working load limit your tie-down needs.

faqs.q: Where is a Grade 80 alloy lashing hook used on a truck or trailer?
faqs.a: It terminates a chain tie-down on a truck, trailer or flatbed, where a load binder tensions the chain to hold cargo. For choosing between chain and strap, read [ratchet strap vs chain and binder](/blog/ratchet-strap-vs-chain-and-binder).

faqs.q: How should I inspect a Grade 80 alloy lashing hook before use?
faqs.a: Look for bending, cracks, wear in the throat and damage to the coating before each use, and take a hook out of service if it is deformed. Lashing fittings need periodic inspection by a competent person.

faqs.q: Do you keep the alloy lashing hook Grade 80 in stock, and how do I order?
faqs.a: Yes, the alloy lashing hook Grade 80 is stocked in our Dubai, UAE warehouse and ships worldwide with the best lead times. For a quotation, send the sizes and quantities via [our contact page](/contact).

faqs.q: What is a chain tension lever and what is it used for?
faqs.a: The chain tension lever is a drop-forged alloy steel tensioner for long-link lashing chain, used to tighten Ro-Ro and general cargo tie-downs. It comes in three sizes, 9, 11 and 13 mm, to match the chain. It is not for overhead lifting.

faqs.q: How do I read the Indus part number on the chain tension lever, for example IH-LR-LB-CTL-9MM?
faqs.a: In IH-LR-LB-CTL-9MM, the suffix 9MM identifies the 9 mm size, and IH-LR-LB-CTL-13MM ends in 13MM for 13 mm. Every size in the size table has its own part number, so quote the one from the table.

faqs.q: Which chain sizes does the chain tension lever fit, and how long is it?
faqs.a: It matches 9 mm, 11 mm and 13 mm chain, one lever per chain size. Overall length L is 575, 585 and 595 mm for the three sizes and weight is 3.4, 4.5 and 5.6 kg. The size table gives the other lettered dimensions.

faqs.q: What breaking load does the chain tension lever carry?
faqs.a: The minimum breaking load is 10,000 kg for the 9 mm size, 15,000 kg for 11 mm and 20,000 kg for 13 mm. No working load limit is published for this lever, so size the tie-down on the chain's lashing capacity and use the lever matched to it.

faqs.q: What is the chain tension lever made from?
faqs.a: It is alloy steel, drop forged and machined, with a powder-coated finish. The design is a lever-action tensioner rather than a ratchet, so it is released by hand with the handle.

faqs.q: Which lashing chain works with the chain tension lever?
faqs.a: Pair it with long-link lashing chain of the same size, such as the [Ro-Ro lashing chain, long link](/p/ro-ro-lashing-chain-long-link) or the [Ro-Ro chain lashing with hook ends](/p/ro-ro-chain-lashing-with-hook-ends), which in turn work with a tension lever of the same chain size.

faqs.q: Does the chain tension lever ship with a test certificate?
faqs.a: Yes. Each consignment ships with the manufacturer's test certificate. The facts we hold name no standard, so state on the RFQ any third-party certification or witnessed testing you need.

faqs.q: Chain tension lever compared with a lever load binder: what is the difference?
faqs.a: The chain tension lever is sized in millimetres for long-link lashing chain, while the [lever load binder](/p/lever-load-binder) is sized by chain range in inches with a working load limit in lbs. Compare them in [lever vs ratchet load binders](/blog/lever-vs-ratchet-load-binder).

faqs.q: Is the chain tension lever safe to release under load?
faqs.a: Release it with care and keep clear of the handle arc, as a lever tensioner stores energy in the handle. This product is a load-securing tool, not lifting equipment. Read the [lever vs ratchet load binder guide](/blog/lever-vs-ratchet-load-binder) before choosing.

faqs.q: Where is a chain tension lever used?
faqs.a: It is used to tension lashing chains that hold vehicles, trailers and cargo units to the deck on Ro-Ro vessels and for general cargo securing. For marine rigging background see [rigging for jetty and marine construction](/blog/jetty-and-marine-construction-rigging).

faqs.q: Can I lift with the chain tension lever?
faqs.a: No. It is listed as not for overhead lifting and is for tensioning tie-downs only. For a lift, use a rated lifting component; tell us the load and we will suggest one.

faqs.q: Do you keep the chain tension lever in stock, and how do I order?
faqs.a: Yes. The chain tension lever is held in stock at our Dubai, UAE warehouse, with worldwide shipping at the best lead times. Request a quote by sending part numbers and quantities through [our contact page](/contact).

faqs.q: What is a claw load binder and what is it used for?
faqs.a: A claw load binder is a lever-action tensioner with claw hook ends for chain tie-downs on trucks and trailers. It is painted red, comes in three sizes from 1/4 to 5/16 in to 3/8 to 1/2 in chain, and is not for lifting.

faqs.q: How do I read the Indus part number on the claw load binder, for example IH-LR-LB-CLAW-025-031?
faqs.a: In IH-LR-LB-CLAW-025-031, the suffix 025-031 identifies the 1/4″-5/16″ size, and IH-LR-LB-CLAW-038-050 ends in 038-050 for 3/8″-1/2″. Every size in the size table has its own part number, so quote the one from the table.

faqs.q: What working load limits does the claw load binder have?
faqs.a: Working load limit is 2,600 lbs for the 1/4 to 5/16 in size, 5,400 lbs for 5/16 to 3/8 in and 9,200 lbs for 3/8 to 1/2 in. Minimum breaking load is 9,200, 19,000 and 33,000 lbs and proof load 5,200, 10,800 and 18,400 lbs.

faqs.q: Which claw load binder size matches which chain?
faqs.a: Match the binder to the chain size and select on working load limit: 1/4 to 5/16 in chain for the 2,600 lbs size, 5/16 to 3/8 in for 5,400 lbs and 3/8 to 1/2 in for 9,200 lbs. Handle length is 290.1, 391.9 and 437.9 mm.

faqs.q: Claw load binder compared with a standard lever load binder: what is different?
faqs.a: The claw binder has three sizes up to 3/8 to 1/2 in chain, while the [lever load binder](/p/lever-load-binder) adds a fourth, larger size. Both use the same ratings for the common sizes. See [lever vs ratchet load binders](/blog/lever-vs-ratchet-load-binder).

faqs.q: Claw load binder compared with a ratchet load binder: which should I buy?
faqs.a: The claw binder is a lever-action tool that tightens fast but stores energy in the handle. The [ratchet load binder](/p/ratchet-load-binder) tensions gradually and releases under control, with eye-end and grab-hook versions. Read [lever vs ratchet load binders](/blog/lever-vs-ratchet-load-binder).

faqs.q: What finish does the claw load binder have?
faqs.a: It is painted red. The facts we hold do not state the steel grade, so confirm the material on the quotation if your specification requires it.

faqs.q: Does the claw load binder come with a certificate?
faqs.a: Yes. Each consignment of claw load binders ships with the manufacturer's test certificate. If your site needs third-party certification or witnessed proof testing, say so on the RFQ.

faqs.q: Can I use a claw load binder for overhead lifting?
faqs.a: No. The claw load binder tensions a chain tie-down to secure a load for transport. Its working load limit is a tensioning rating, and it is not for lifting.

faqs.q: How should I use and release a claw load binder safely?
faqs.a: Keep the handle under control when tensioning and releasing, because a lever binder stores energy in the handle. Inspect the claws and handle before each use and take it out of service if bent. The [lever vs ratchet guide](/blog/lever-vs-ratchet-load-binder) covers the kickback hazard.

faqs.q: Where are claw load binders used?
faqs.a: They tension chain tie-downs on flatbed trucks and trailers carrying equipment, pipe, timber and machinery. Compare chain and strap securing in [ratchet strap vs chain and binder](/blog/ratchet-strap-vs-chain-and-binder).

faqs.q: Do you keep the claw load binder in stock, and how do I order?
faqs.a: Yes. We keep the claw load binder in stock at our warehouse in Dubai, UAE, and ship worldwide with the best lead times. Send the size and quantity through [our contact page](/contact) for a quotation.

faqs.q: What is the Grade 100 ratchet load binder and what is it used for?
faqs.a: The Grade 100 ratchet load binder is a powder-coated alloy steel ratchet tensioner built to the EN 12195-3 pattern for tension, lashing and fixing duty. It comes in 9 sizes from 50 to 134 kN and is not for overhead lifting.

faqs.q: How do I read the Indus part number on the Grade 100 ratchet load binder, for example IH-LR-LB-100RLB-50KN-SH?
faqs.a: In IH-LR-LB-100RLB-50KN-SH, the suffix 50KN-SH identifies the 50 kN size, and IH-LR-LB-100RLB-134KN-WH ends in 134KN-WH for 134 kN. Every size in the size table has its own part number, so quote the one from the table. The last letters give the end type: SH safety hooks, CE clevis ends, WH without hooks.

faqs.q: Which end types does the Grade 100 ratchet load binder come with?
faqs.a: It is available with safety hooks, clevis ends or without hooks, each in 50, 80 and 134 kN. The extension runs from 340 to 365 mm minimum length to 500 to 525 mm maximum, depending on size. The size table has the lettered dimensions per type.

faqs.q: What are the lashing capacity and breaking load of the Grade 100 ratchet load binder?
faqs.a: Lashing capacity is 50, 80 and 134 kN, with minimum breaking load 100, 160 and 268 kN. The binder is rated with a 2:1 design factor between working load limit and minimum breaking load. Select on lashing capacity.

faqs.q: How heavy is the Grade 100 ratchet load binder in each type?
faqs.a: Weights differ by type. The 50 kN size weighs 3.71 kg with safety hooks and 2.6 kg with clevis ends or without hooks; the 134 kN size weighs 9.34 kg, 5 kg and 5 kg respectively. The size table lists all nine rows.

faqs.q: What standard does the Grade 100 ratchet load binder follow?
faqs.a: It is built to the EN 12195-3 pattern. The facts we hold do not describe third-party certification, so state any certificate you need on the RFQ.

faqs.q: What is the Grade 100 ratchet load binder made of?
faqs.a: It is drop-forged and machined alloy steel with a powder-coated finish. Grade 100 is the higher alloy grade compared with the [Grade 80 ratchet load binder (EN 12195-3)](/p/grade-80-ratchet-load-binder-en-12195-3).

faqs.q: Grade 100 ratchet load binder compared with Grade 80: which should I choose?
faqs.a: The Grade 100 binder reaches 134 kN lashing capacity in 9 sizes. The [Grade 80 ratchet binder to EN 12195-3](/p/grade-80-ratchet-load-binder-en-12195-3) is listed with safety hooks only. Choose on the rating your lashing needs, and keep the chain grade matched.

faqs.q: What chain and hooks work with the Grade 100 ratchet load binder?
faqs.a: Use it with chain and end fittings of the matching grade, with the binder ends chosen from safety hooks, clevis ends or no hooks. For hook-end options see the [Grade 80 winch hook with half link and safety latch](/p/grade-80-winch-hook-half-link-safety-latch).

faqs.q: Can the Grade 100 ratchet load binder be used for lifting?
faqs.a: No. The manufacturer rates this range for tension, lashing or fixing and states it is not for overhead lifting. For a lift, use a rated lifting component; tell us the load and we will suggest one.

faqs.q: Ratchet or lever: why choose the Grade 100 ratchet load binder?
faqs.a: A ratchet binder tensions gradually and releases under control, so it suits operators who tension and release often. A lever binder is quicker but stores energy in the handle. See [lever vs ratchet load binders](/blog/lever-vs-ratchet-load-binder).

faqs.q: Do you keep the Grade 100 ratchet load binder in stock, and how do I order?
faqs.a: Yes, the Grade 100 ratchet load binder is stocked in our Dubai, UAE warehouse and ships worldwide with the best lead times. For a quotation, send the sizes and quantities via [our contact page](/contact).

faqs.q: What is a Grade 80 lashing type C hook with spring pin?
faqs.a: It is a drop-forged alloy steel hook with a spring pin for chain tie-downs that secure a load for transport. It comes in three sizes, 2.5, 3.75 and 5.4 t, and is not for overhead lifting.

faqs.q: How do I read the Indus part number on the Grade 80 lashing type C hook with spring pin, for example IH-LR-LB-G80LCHSP-2P5T?
faqs.a: In IH-LR-LB-G80LCHSP-2P5T, the suffix 2P5T identifies the 2.5 t size, and IH-LR-LB-G80LCHSP-5P4T ends in 5P4T for 5.4 t. Every size in the size table has its own part number, so quote the one from the table. Here P stands for the decimal point.

faqs.q: What are the working load limits of the Grade 80 lashing type C hook?
faqs.a: Working load limit is 2.5, 3.75 and 5.4 t, with minimum breaking load 10, 15 and 21.6 t. That is a 4:1 ratio between breaking load and working load limit. Select the hook on its working load limit.

faqs.q: What are the dimensions and weights of the Grade 80 lashing type C hook sizes?
faqs.a: Weight is 0.5 kg for 2.5 t, 0.85 kg for 3.75 t and 1.38 kg for 5.4 t. Overall length L is 143, 177 and 205 mm. The size table lists A, B, L and R for the dimension drawing.

faqs.q: What is the Grade 80 lashing type C hook made of, and how is it finished?
faqs.a: It is drop-forged alloy steel with a powder-coated finish. The Grade 80 designation indicates the chain grade it is intended for. Match the chain, hook and binder ratings.

faqs.q: Does the Grade 80 lashing type C hook come with a test certificate?
faqs.a: Yes. Each consignment ships with the manufacturer's test certificate. The facts do not name a standard, so state on the RFQ if you need witnessed proof testing or third-party certification.

faqs.q: Grade 80 lashing type C hook compared with the alloy lashing hook Grade 80?
faqs.a: The type C hook with spring pin is the larger part at 2.5 to 5.4 t in three sizes, while the [alloy lashing hook Grade 80](/p/alloy-lashing-hook-grade-80) is a single 1 t size. Choose on the working load limit your tie-down needs.

faqs.q: What does the Grade 80 lashing type C hook connect to?
faqs.a: It ends a Grade 80 chain tie-down and is tensioned by a load binder such as the [ratchet load binder (EN 12195-3)](/p/grade-80-ratchet-load-binder-en-12195-3). Match the chain size and the rating of every part in the tie-down.

faqs.q: Can the Grade 80 lashing type C hook be used for overhead lifting?
faqs.a: No. It is listed as not for overhead lifting, and its working load limit is a lashing rating. Use a rated lifting component for a lift; ask us which one.

faqs.q: How do I check a type C hook with spring pin before use?
faqs.a: Check that the spring pin closes and holds, look for cracks, bending and wear in the hook and replace any hook that has opened up. Lashing fittings need periodic inspection by a competent person.

faqs.q: Where is the lashing type C hook used?
faqs.a: It terminates chain lashings for securing vehicles, machinery and cargo on flatbed trucks and trailers. See [ratchet strap vs chain and binder](/blog/ratchet-strap-vs-chain-and-binder) for when chain is the better choice.

faqs.q: Do you keep the Grade 80 lashing type C hook with spring pin in stock, and how do I order?

faqs.q: What is the Grade 80 ratchet load binder to EN 12195-3?
faqs.a: It is a powder-coated alloy steel ratchet binder with safety hooks, built to the EN 12195-3 pattern for tension, lashing and fixing duty. It comes in 4 sizes from 40 to 160 kN and is not for overhead lifting.

faqs.q: How do I read the Indus part number on the Grade 80 ratchet load binder (EN 12195-3), for example IH-LR-LB-80RLBE121-40KN?
faqs.a: In IH-LR-LB-80RLBE121-40KN, the suffix 40KN identifies the 40 kN size, and IH-LR-LB-80RLBE121-160KN ends in 160KN for 160 kN. Every size in the size table has its own part number, so quote the one from the table.

faqs.q: What are the working load limits and breaking loads of the Grade 80 EN 12195-3 ratchet binder?
faqs.a: Working load limit is 40, 63, 100 and 160 kN, with minimum breaking load 80.4, 126, 212 and 322 kN. Select the size on the working load limit and match it to the chain.

faqs.q: What are the dimensions and weights of the Grade 80 ratchet binder sizes?
faqs.a: Weight is 3.18 kg for 40 kN, 5.3 kg for 63 kN, 8.4 kg for 100 kN and 8.8 kg for 160 kN. Minimum length is 340, 365 or 390 mm and maximum length 500, 525 or 550 mm depending on size.

faqs.q: Which standard does the Grade 80 ratchet load binder follow?
faqs.a: It is built to the EN 12195-3 pattern. The facts we hold do not describe third-party certification, so state any certificate you need on the RFQ.

faqs.q: What is the Grade 80 EN 12195-3 ratchet binder made of?
faqs.a: It is alloy steel with a powder-coated finish and safety hooks on every listed size. Safety hooks close the throat to stop the chain slipping out when the load moves.

faqs.q: Grade 80 ratchet binder compared with the Grade 100 ratchet binder?
faqs.a: The [Grade 100 ratchet load binder](/p/grade-100-ratchet-load-binder) offers three end types, while this Grade 80 binder has safety hooks on all 4 sizes. Select on the rated capacity you need.

faqs.q: Grade 80 EN 12195-3 ratchet binder compared with the AS/NZS 4344 ratchet binder?
faqs.a: This binder is rated in kN, while the [AS/NZS 4344 ratchet binder](/p/ratchet-load-binder-as-nzs-4344) is rated in kg lashing capacity. Choose the standard your site or destination specifies.

faqs.q: What do I connect the Grade 80 ratchet load binder to?
faqs.a: It tensions Grade 80 lashing chain through its safety hooks, with end fittings such as the [Grade 80 winch hook with half link and safety latch](/p/grade-80-winch-hook-half-link-safety-latch). Check every part of the tie-down is rated for the load.

faqs.q: Can I use the Grade 80 ratchet load binder for lifting?

faqs.q: Why choose a ratchet binder over a lever binder for chain tie-downs?
faqs.a: A ratchet binder tensions gradually and releases under control, so it suits operators who tension and release often. Read [lever vs ratchet load binders](/blog/lever-vs-ratchet-load-binder) for the kickback hazard of lever binders.

faqs.q: Do you keep the Grade 80 ratchet load binder in stock, and how do I order?

faqs.q: What is a Grade 80 winch hook with half link and safety latch?
faqs.a: It is a drop-forged, quenched and tempered alloy steel hook with a half link and safety latch for chain tie-downs that secure a load. It comes in 7 sizes from 6 to 22 mm with working load limits of 1.12 to 15 t and is not for lifting.

faqs.q: How do I read the Indus part number on the Grade 80 winch hook with half link and safety latch, for example IH-LR-LB-G80WHHLSL-6MM?
faqs.a: In IH-LR-LB-G80WHHLSL-6MM, the suffix 6MM identifies the 6 mm size, and IH-LR-LB-G80WHHLSL-22MM ends in 22MM for 22 mm. Every size in the size table has its own part number, so quote the one from the table.

faqs.q: What working load limits does the Grade 80 winch hook half link have?
faqs.a: Working load limit is 1.12 t for 6 mm, 2 t for 8 mm, 3.15 t for 10 mm, 5.3 t for 13 mm, 8 t for 16 mm, 12.5 t for 20 mm and 15 t for 22 mm. Minimum breaking load runs from 4.48 to 60 t.

faqs.q: What are the dimensions and weights of the Grade 80 winch hook sizes?
faqs.a: Weight rises from 0.35 kg at 6 mm to 12 kg at 22 mm, with 8 mm at 0.47 kg, 10 mm at 1.3 kg, 13 mm at 3 kg, 16 mm at 4.4 kg and 20 mm at 7.3 kg. The size table lists the lettered dimensions.

faqs.q: How is the Grade 80 winch hook half link made?
faqs.a: The hook is drop forged, quenched and tempered alloy steel with a powder-coated finish. The safety latch closes the throat to keep the chain or ring in the hook when the tie-down slackens.

faqs.q: Does the Grade 80 winch hook come with a certificate?
faqs.a: Yes. Each consignment ships with the manufacturer's test certificate. State any third-party certification or witnessed proof testing you need on the RFQ.

faqs.q: Grade 80 winch hook compared with the 3.5T carbon steel winch hook with latch?
faqs.a: This hook is alloy Grade 80 with published working load limits in 7 sizes. The [winch hook with latch, carbon steel 3.5T](/p/winch-hook-with-latch-carbon-steel-3-5t) is a single 19 mm carbon steel hook with no published load rating.

faqs.q: What does the Grade 80 winch hook connect to?
faqs.a: It attaches to a Grade 80 chain through its half link and is tensioned with a binder such as the [Grade 80 ratchet load binder](/p/grade-80-ratchet-load-binder-en-12195-3). Match chain size and ratings.

faqs.q: Can the Grade 80 winch hook be used for overhead lifting?

faqs.q: How do I inspect a winch hook with safety latch?

faqs.q: Where is a Grade 80 winch hook used?

faqs.q: Do you keep the Grade 80 winch hook with half link and safety latch in stock, and how do I order?

faqs.q: What is a lever load binder and what is it used for?
faqs.a: A lever load binder is a lever-action tensioner for chain tie-downs on trucks and trailers. It is painted red and comes in 4 sizes from 1/4 to 5/16 in up to 1/2 to 5/8 in chain, with working load limits of 2,600 to 13,000 lbs. It is not for lifting.

faqs.q: How do I read the Indus part number on the lever load binder, for example IH-LR-LB-LEV-025-031?
faqs.a: In IH-LR-LB-LEV-025-031, the suffix 025-031 identifies the 1/4″-5/16″ size, and IH-LR-LB-LEV-050-062 ends in 050-062 for 1/2″-5/8″. Every size in the size table has its own part number, so quote the one from the table.

faqs.q: What working load limits does the lever load binder have?
faqs.a: Working load limit is 2,600, 5,400, 9,200 and 13,000 lbs across the four sizes, with minimum breaking load 9,200, 19,000, 33,000 and 46,000 lbs. Proof load is 5,200, 10,800, 18,400 and 26,000 lbs.

faqs.q: Which lever load binder size matches which chain size, and what is the take-up?
faqs.a: Match the size to the chain: 1/4 to 5/16 in for 2,600 lbs through to 1/2 to 5/8 in for 13,000 lbs. Take-up is 114.3, 120.6 and 95.2 mm across the sizes and handle length runs from 290.1 to 533.4 mm.

faqs.q: Lever load binder compared with a ratchet load binder?
faqs.a: A lever binder is quick but stores energy in the handle and must be released with care. The [ratchet load binder](/p/ratchet-load-binder) tensions gradually and releases under control. See [lever vs ratchet load binders](/blog/lever-vs-ratchet-load-binder).

faqs.q: Lever load binder compared with the recoil-less lever load binder, Grade 70?
faqs.a: The [recoil-less lever binder, Grade 70](/p/recoil-less-lever-load-binder-grade-70) is a single size built to the US federal specification, designed to reduce handle kickback. This standard lever binder has four sizes.

faqs.q: What finish does the lever load binder have?
faqs.a: It is painted red. The facts we hold do not state the steel grade, so confirm the material on the quotation if your specification requires it.

faqs.q: Does the lever load binder come with a test certificate?
faqs.a: Yes. Each consignment ships with the manufacturer's test certificate. Say on the RFQ if your site needs third-party certification or witnessed proof testing.

faqs.q: Can the lever load binder be used for lifting?
faqs.a: No. A load binder tensions a chain tie-down to secure a load for transport. Its working load limit is a tensioning rating and it is not for lifting.

faqs.q: How do I release a lever load binder safely?
